highest_reported.source_location: Bondarenko, Radchenko, and Viazovska (2013), p. 444: 24 minimal vectors of D4 form a spherical 5-design in S^3
highest_reported.reproduction_status: The 24-cell vertices are frozen as exact rational coordinates and the checker verifies unit norms and all 126 equal-weight polynomial moments through degree five. This is a feasible upper bound; it does not prove minimality.
highest_reported.ai_provenance: Classical D4 root-system construction; no AI provenance stated.

parameters.coordinate_domain: real algebraic coordinates in one common real algebraic number field

known_bounds.upper_bound_location: p. 444: the 24 D4 minimal vectors form a spherical 5-design
known_bounds.status: The exact value is open in sources checked on 2026-11-06. The 2025 paper calls the 24-point design putatively optimal but gives no proof of the finite minimum.

2025_status_source.source_location: §3 near Table 1: the 24-point 5-design on S^3 is described as putatively optimally small; the paper states only t=1,2,3 are known optimal in S^3 among those constructions
2025_status_source.interpretation: Supports continued conjectural status; it is not a proof that 24 is minimum.

adjacent_2026_sources.scope: Proves minimum 12 for equal-weight spherical 4-designs on S^2; not the selected S^3 strength-5 problem.
Constructs spherical designs in odd dimensions including S^3; it does not give a matching lower bound for N(3,5).

coordinate_model.scope: The task accepts points over any common real algebraic number field, with a primitive irreducible polynomial and rational isolating interval.
coordinate_model.completeness_note: This representation does not change the minimum over real coordinates: for each fixed finite point count, the unit-sphere and moment equations plus pairwise-distinct inequalities form a semialgebraic set over Q. Any nonempty such set has a real algebraic point, which can be represented in a common primitive number field.
coordinate_model.input_caps: No arbitrary degree or coefficient-size cap; shared runner output, time, and memory budgets apply.

independent_quantity.method: symbolic real-root coordinates and Dirichlet rising-factorial sphere moments
